title: Art Books on Needles and Threads
summary: We recommend titles on fiber art, weaving, and textiles, plus Megan O’Grady on a new John Berger biography.

title: Hundreds Protest in Colombia After Far-Right President Removes Works From National Museum
summary: In a Trumpian move, the government of Abelardo de la Espriella took down works referencing LGBTQ+ and women’s rights and political violence.

title: Gowanus Open Studios Turns 30
summary: This year’s iteration of the artistic assembly was a love letter to the neighborhood and its craftsmanship amid an era of remediation, development, and gentrification.

title: Beer With a Painter: Melissa Brown
summary: “I want to visualize the fact that, despite our perception, reality is changeable,” the Brooklyn-based artist said of her paintings.

title: David Reed Went Where Lichtenstein Wouldn’t
summary: He brought his optical preoccupations into the 21st century, without losing his love of artists from earlier eras.

title: Let’s Give a Round of A-Paws to These Tompkins Dog Parade Participants
summary: Santa Paws, Vincent van Doge, and the papal Pup Leo were among this year’s fierce competition.

title: Paris Students Block Louvre Entrance, Forcing Closure
summary: Students from the independent École du Louvre and the National School of Fine Arts are leading the ongoing action.

title: Rosana Paulino Reads the Archive Against Those Who Made It
summary: “This history is dirty,” says the Brazilian artist, who sees the colonial past as an active force in her country’s present.

title: This Iranian Documentary Wasn’t Meant to Begin This Way
summary: In Mani Haghighi’s new film, an artist’s extensive archive draws the ire of the authorities.

title: Diasporican Abstraction: A Cross-Border Cartography of Puerto Rican Abstraction
summary: More than sixty artists explore migration, memory, and identity in this survey of Puerto Rican abstraction across and beyond the archipelago.

title: Smiles Meyer Queers “The Last Supper”
summary: The Los Angeles-based photographer, who was raised in a conservative Catholic environment, is reclaiming the divinity of queer and trans identity through religious imagery.

title: The Buffalo Haunts America
summary: Hrag Vartanian on Cannupa Hanska Luger, Artavazd Pelechian’s cinema of connections, and a Ron DeSantis statue melts.

title: Diaries of a Primitive Man
summary: John Yau on Roy Lichtenstein, Megan O’Grady on John Berger, and Paddy Johnson answers the question: Do I need an agent?

title: Cannupa Hanska Luger’s Truth About America
summary: The beauty of the Native artist’s forms seduces, but the visual history of destruction is embedded into each element.

title: Artavazd Pelechian’s Distant Connections
summary: Through his “distance montage” technique, the Armenian filmmaker’s masterpieces are built around impressions, not stories.
